headline: Medium risk: shared-file and output-chaining pathways exist, but both tools are offline/local and no direct injection or compliance breach is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI can read filesystem inputs and Great Expectations can consume files for validation results/documentation, so a shared workspace could let attacker-controlled content flow from agent_a into agent_b as trusted instructions. Neither profile shows clipboard/MCP bridging or direct parser hardening, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, THEN file content from agent_a can reach agent_b.
IF agent_b parses agent_a-produced text as configuration or documentation, THEN prompt-like content can influence behavior.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories.
Rename or quarantine any agent_a outputs before agent_b reads them.
Add a manual review step for any text files passed between agents.
Use read-only mounts for agent_b inputs where possible.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for inter-agent files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents are open-source and documented as offline or no-egress by default, so leakage to third parties is limited. The remaining risk is local workspace exposure: agent_a can touch model files and agent_b can read/write validation artifacts, but no profile shows shared sensitive data or outbound upload by default.
conditions: IF the same local workspace contains sensitive files, THEN both agents may expose them through their file surfaces.
IF operator copies secrets into validation artifacts or model assets, THEN those secrets can persist locally.
mitigations: Keep sensitive data out of the shared workspace.
Use separate OS users for each agent.
Delete temporary artifacts after each run.
Restrict file permissions on input/output folders.
requires-engineering: add automatic secret scanning before handoff.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, while agent_b can install packages but has no documented write or git capability. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; the main overlap is read/file handling, so the pair is not strongly conflicting.
conditions: IF agent_b is wrapped by an external orchestrator that grants write access, THEN conflicts could emerge.
IF both agents are given the same mutable dependency directory, THEN package or artifact drift may occur.
mitigations: Keep package installs isolated from shared project files.
Pin dependencies before running agent_b.
Avoid giving agent_a any write-capable wrapper.
Run each agent in its own working directory.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A plausible workflow is agent_a generating images or workflow artifacts that agent_b then documents or validates. Because agent_b has no built-in verification of agent_a's semantics in the profile, A's output could become B's input without a strong check, creating a moderate cascading-error pathway.
conditions: IF agent_b is tasked to validate or document outputs produced by agent_a, THEN unverified assumptions can propagate.
IF agent_a emits malformed workflow metadata, THEN agent_b may preserve the error in validation results or docs.
mitigations: Require a human spot-check of agent_a outputs before agent_b uses them.
Add schema validation on any handoff files.
Keep agent_b outputs clearly labeled as derived, not authoritative.
Use a checksum or manifest for transferred artifacts.
requires-engineering: add automated cross-checks against source data.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source, docs-only, and show no special residency, certification, or retention claims. With no evidence of regulated data classes or cross-border transfer, compliance risk is limited to local policy mismatches rather than a documented breach pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data is manually placed into either agent's workspace, THEN local policy obligations may apply.
IF the operator requires retention limits, THEN generated artifacts must be deleted manually.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in either workspace.
Document a local retention rule for outputs.
Delete temporary files after review.
Keep audit logs separate from content files.
requires-engineering: formalize residency and retention controls.
